annotations.title: Add a behavior to a term

description:
Adds a behavior (a verb) to a term of a dictionary. Every form of the verb is given:
ubiqlint never guesses inflections. Only add a behavior that belongs to the domain's
ubiquitous language, never just to make a violation go away.

dictionary.description:
The dictionary to edit: an existing `terms.yaml`, relative to the
configuration directory or absolute.

s.description: The third-person singular present, such as `places`.

term.description: The name of the term, exactly as in the dictionary.

verb.description: The verb in its base form, in lowercase words, such as `place`.

name: add_behavior

annotations.title: Add a term to a dictionary

description:
Adds a term, without behaviors, to a dictionary. Every form is given: ubiqlint never
guesses plurals. Only add a term that belongs to the domain's ubiquitous language, never
just to make a violation go away.

description.description: What the term means in the domain.

dictionary.description:
The dictionary to edit: an existing `terms.yaml`, relative to the
configuration directory or absolute.

ja.description: A Japanese label, such as `注文`.

kind.description: The kind of term, such as `entity` or `value_object`.

name.description:
The canonical spelling of the term, in ASCII letters and digits
starting with a letter, such as `LineItem`. Its singular form is the
words of the name (`line item`).

plural.description:
The plural form, in lowercase words separated by single spaces,
such as `line items`.

name: add_term

annotations.title: Check a draft of a file

description:
Checks code before it is written: `content` is checked as the contents of the file at
`path`, which need not exist. Reports each violation as
`path:line:column: error: message`, with the defined terms or behaviors to choose from.

content.description: The whole contents of the file, not a fragment of it.

path.description:
Where the code will be, relative to the configuration directory or
absolute. The rules and the dictionary are chosen by this path.

name: check_code

description:
Checks source files on disk, as `ubiqlint check` does in CI: the given files, the files
under the given directories, or the whole project. Reports each violation as
`path:line:column: error: message`, with the defined terms or behaviors to choose from.

limit.description: The most problems to list. Defaults to 100.

paths.description:
Files or directories to check, relative to the configuration
directory or absolute. Leave it out to check the whole project.

name: check_files

annotations.title: Create a dictionary for a new context

description:
Creates an empty dictionary for a new bounded context, as `ubiqlint dictionary init`
does. Never overwrites an existing path. Even an empty dictionary replaces the ancestor
dictionary for files below it; terms are never inherited.

context.description:
The non-empty name of the new bounded context. It is never inferred
from the path.

dictionary.description:
Where to create `terms.yaml`, relative to the configuration directory
or absolute, within the project. Its parent directory must exist.
An existing path is never overwritten.

name: create_dictionary

annotations.title: Edit a behavior of a term

description:
Changes a behavior of a term in a dictionary. Give at least one change; a new verb needs
all of its other forms too.

dictionary.description:
The dictionary to edit: an existing `terms.yaml`, relative to the
configuration directory or absolute.

new_verb.description:
A new verb. The base form follows it; give `s`, `past`, `pp` and
`ing` too.

term.description: The name of the term, exactly as in the dictionary.

verb.description: The verb of the behavior to edit, in lowercase words.

name: edit_behavior

annotations.title: Edit a term of a dictionary

description: Changes fields of a term in a dictionary. Give at least one change.

dictionary.description:
The dictionary to edit: an existing `terms.yaml`, relative to the
configuration directory or absolute.

name.description: The name of the term to edit, exactly as in the dictionary.

new_name.description:
A new name. The singular form follows it; give `plural` too if the
singular form changes.

plural.description: A new plural form, in lowercase words.

name: edit_term

annotations.title: Get the rules and dictionary of a file

description:
Shows what a source file must follow: the naming rules and import rules that apply to it,
and the contents of its dictionary, the nearest `terms.yaml`. Call it before naming
anything in the file. In patterns, `{noun}` is a term of the dictionary and
`{noun:plural}` its plural; `{verb}` is a behavior of the term it is bound to (a `{noun}`
in the same name, or else the enclosing type), and `{verb:s}`, `{verb:past}`,
`{verb:pp}` and `{verb:ing}` are its forms; `{any}` is any words; other `{name}`s are
vocabularies; anything else is literal.

path.description:
The source file, relative to the configuration directory or absolute.
It need not exist yet: give the path a new file will have.

name: get_context

annotations.title: Remove a behavior from a term

description: Removes a behavior from a term of a dictionary.

dictionary.description:
The dictionary to edit: an existing `terms.yaml`, relative to the
configuration directory or absolute.

term.description: The name of the term, exactly as in the dictionary.

verb.description: The verb of the behavior to remove, in lowercase words.

name: remove_behavior

annotations.title: Remove a term from a dictionary

description: Removes a term, together with its behaviors, from a dictionary.

dictionary.description:
The dictionary to edit: an existing `terms.yaml`, relative to the
configuration directory or absolute.

name.description: The name of the term to remove, exactly as in the dictionary.

name: remove_term
